newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lamfalussy - euro to live up to stability hopes.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy - euro to live up to stability hopes.

text.p: President of the European Monetary Institute, Alexandre Lamfalussy, said on Wednesday that the planned single European currency unit, the euro, would be a very stable currency.

"The euro will fulfil the high stability expectations which everyone has for the planned single currency," Lamfalussy said at a ceremony in Berlin, where he received an award for his services as EMI President from the German President Roman Herzog.
European currency union is due to begin on January 1, 1999, with as many nations as meet the strict entry criteria.
The long-term credibility of the currency would only come about if the political context was fitting, Lamfalussy said.
Lamfalussy will leave his post in June, to be replaced by Wim Duisenberg, head of the Dutch central bank.
